confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly states that each participant was randomly assigned to one of two conditions, supporting individual, between-person assignment; condition-order randomization is not applicable.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1, Human Study, first paragraph; p. 22, Appendix A.3-A.4.

confirmed.statement: The assigned arms were a no-LLM control (n = 45) and an AI-assisted condition with embedded gpt-4o-mini access (n = 55).
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1, Human Study, assignment sentence.

confirmed.statement: Participants could use the embedded LLM however they chose while writing their own essay; the researchers recorded the interaction history and final draft.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1, Human Study; p. 22, Appendix A.3, LLM Assisted Instructions.

confirmed.statement: The writing tool is identified as an LLM, gpt-4o-mini; the sample conversation shows generation of essay paragraphs in response to participant prompts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1, Human Study; p. 55, Appendix H.1, participant requests for introductory and financial-stress paragraphs and the LLM responses.

confirmed.statement: Control instructions prohibit LLMs, AI assistants, and internet use. AI-condition instructions allow the provided LLM chat and prohibit other LLMs and outside sources.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 22, Appendix A.3, LLM Assisted Instructions, and A.4, Without LLM Instructions.

confirmed.statement: The LLM-Influenced and LLM groups classify actual use within the AI-access arm; they are not additional randomized arms, as the form correctly records.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, paragraph beginning Before running the full experiment, following the two-arm assignment on p. 4.

confirmed.statement: The usage classification was determined before results analysis: LLM-Influenced required self-reported generation of less than 40% of the text, checked against the essay and interaction transcript.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, pilot and primary-study classification paragraph.

confirmed.statement: The paper reports 28 of 55 AI-access users classified as LLM-Influenced and 12 of 55 refusing LLM essay generation; neither count is presented as a separately randomized arm.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, final two sentences of the pilot and primary-study classification paragraph.

confirmed.statement: gpt-4o was used separately as an LLM-as-a-Judge to classify essays, consistent with the form distinguishing it from the gpt-4o-mini writing assistant.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.2, Qualitative Analyses Using LLM-as-a-Judge; p. 4, Section 3.1, Human Study.

summary: S1 explicitly randomized people to write an essay with embedded gpt-4o-mini access or without AI, so criterion 1 holds. The form correctly distinguishes that assignment from the subsequent classification by actual LLM use, and no assignment-coding error was found.
